documents.title: Complete AI Guidelines
documents.summary: Provost guidelines for the whole community covering principles, data protection, verification and disclosure, then separate sections for students, instructors, researchers and administrative staff. For students, AI is banned on assignments and exams unless the syllabus grants permission.
documents.stance_why: The student section says 'Unless an instructor includes a clear statement in their syllabus granting permission, the use of generative AI tools to complete an assignment or exam is prohibited', which is a ban unless permitted. Instructors set the permissions, but the university sets this default, so restrict rather than delegates.

documents.title: Academic Integrity Policy
documents.summary: A general academic integrity policy and adjudication process in which AI appears in the definitions of cheating and plagiarism and in the faculty duty to put an AI statement on syllabi. Most of the text is procedure for all incidents, and a few units are coded because they apply to AI cases.
documents.stance_why: Cheating covers AI 'not authorized by the instructor' and plagiarism covers AI-produced work 'without proper citation', so AI is barred unless authorized or cited, which is restrict.

units.why: Students must practice 'Acknowledging the source of information whether taken from another person, artificial intelligence, or other technology', a duty to acknowledge AI as a source, P24.
units.anchor: Acknowledging the source of information whether taken from another person, artificial intelligence, or other technology.
units.frag_start: Acknowledging the source of information

units.why: Cheating includes using AI 'not authorized by the instructor' in quizzes, exams or assignments, so unauthorized AI is misconduct (P36) and AI needs instructor authorization.
units.anchor: applications not authorized by the instructor in taking quizzes or examinations or to complete assignments
units.frag_start: Using assistance, notes, aids, artificial intelligence
units.policy: Using artificial intelligence not authorized by the instructor in taking quizzes or examinations or to complete assignments is cheating.

units.why: Plagiarism includes presenting work 'generated or created by ... artificial intelligence' without quotation marks and citation, so uncited AI text is misconduct, P36.
units.anchor: created by someone other than the student, by artificial intelligence, or by other technology
units.frag_start: Directly presenting the written, artistic, or spoken work

units.why: Plagiarism includes paraphrasing material generated by AI 'without proper citation of the source', P36.
units.anchor: by artificial intelligence, or by other technology without proper citation of the source.
units.frag_start: Paraphrasing or incorporating the ideas

units.frag_start: Presenting information from the internet

units.why: Plagiarism includes submitting work 'prepared, either entirely or in part, by ... artificial intelligence ... without proper citation', so uncited AI-prepared work is misconduct, P36.
units.anchor: prepared, either entirely or in part, by another person, group, commercial firm, artificial intelligence
units.frag_start: Submitting as the student's own, any work

units.anchor: an explicit statement on use of artificial intelligence and/or other technology
units.frag_start: sharing relevant parts of the policy on their syllabi
units.frag_end: and out of their academic unit.

units.why: Findings are decided on a preponderance of evidence, 'more likely than not', based on 'the totality of the information'; this evidence standard governs AI misuse findings too, P69.
units.anchor: based on the totality of the information or materials available to the decision maker(s)
